records.text: Summary and recommended direction Build an MIT engine around NoGraphicsAPI’s data model, prove hardware ray tracing and reconstruction early, and grow scene detail through streaming. UE5.8 is a visual target; UE6 is a roadmap to track. Recommendation · architecture with an initial tested foundation Start with a Windows Vulkan vertical slice using a pinned NoGraphicsAPI fork. Add narrow RT and native SDK interoperability extensions. Keep original Basix renderer code under MIT. Offer NVIDIA SDK adapters as optional components with separate terms and a working non-DLSS path. This is feasible as a focused renderer and game framework. Matching UE’s complete engine, tools and content ecosystem is a much larger effort. NoGraphicsAPI reduces binding/API complexity; it does not supply scene streaming, a material system, ray tracing, denoising or an editor. The first milestone must test the missing RT/SDK seam before major engine investment. Evidence boundary: public documentation, license texts and the pinned NoGraphicsAPI source were inspected. An initial NoGraphicsAPI/Vulkan hardware-ray-query experiment and CPU cage math are implemented and locally tested. No performance benchmark or UE visual parity has been demonstrated. records.text: UE5.8 and UE6: define the benchmark Epic released UE5.8 in June 2026. Its rendering overview makes MegaLights production-ready and introduces lower-cost Lumen Lite GI. Geometry/worldbuilding features have separate maturity labels; do not treat everything in the release as production-ready. Epic targets UE6 Early Access at the end of 2027 and full release 12–18 months afterward. That is a target, and the development stream is not an alpha. S07 · S08 UE capability Basix requirement / proposed equivalent First useful scope Nanite-like detail Cluster hierarchy, LOD error bounds, GPU culling and geometry streaming; maintain a compatible RT representation. Conventional meshlets and explicit LODs before virtualized microgeometry. Lumen-like GI Dynamic bounce lighting with stable temporal reconstruction and disocclusion recovery. Probe/cached diffuse GI for hybrid mode; independent full PT reference. MegaLights Stochastic many-light direct illumination with soft visibility. Analytic area lights plus emissive triangle sampling; inspect selected samples and visibility. Material richness Consistent energy-aware BSDF evaluation and texture LOD in raster and ray paths. Metallic/roughness, normal maps, emissive and alpha test; later layered materials and transmission. Large worlds Camera-relative coordinates, cell streaming, dependency-aware asset cooking and residency. One dense district or indoor/outdoor scene with bounded memory. Development speed Deterministic asset builds, shader cache, crash diagnostics and hot reload. Scene inspector and reproducible capture runner before a general editor. Reasoning: “UE-like” must be converted into scene-level acceptance criteria. A close-up scanned prop, an emissive city interior and a forest stress very different systems. High triangle count alone cannot establish parity. Use self-created or separately licensed assets, a fixed camera and material/light calibration; include a path-traced reference in comparisons.

records.text: NoGraphicsAPI: adopt the model, expose the gaps The pinned upstream implementation uses C++20 and shared Slang shaders on Vulkan and Metal. It is MIT, with separate third-party notices. Vulkan 1.4 alone is insufficient: the README requires descriptor heaps, mesh shaders and untyped shader pointers. Its compatibility table is a dated report, not a promise about every current driver. Pin the toolchain and enumerate device features on startup. S01 · S25 Source inspection of NoGraphicsAPI.hpp at ffd9f2ab… finds draw/compute/mesh, heap, queue and synchronization APIs, but no public BLAS/TLAS construction, ray pipeline dispatch or native-handle SDK interface. Hardware triangle RT therefore requires implementation work. Compute dispatch can host software tracing, but does not by itself expose hardware traversal. S02 Keep the pointer-root approach, application-owned allocation and indexed texture heaps. Protect root addresses and descriptor slots until GPU completion. Roots use a shared constant-buffer ABI, while pointed-to data uses C POD layout; enforce C++ offsets and compiled shader reflection in CI. Upstream synchronization omits per-resource lists, but Basix still needs resource knowledge for lifetime, aliasing, SDK state contracts and scheduling. S03 · S04 Proposed Basix extension Responsibilities / proof required RayScene / RayBackend BLAS/TLAS size queries, scratch allocation, build/update/compact, instance masks, AABB geometry, and build-to-trace synchronization. Trace a static triangle and a moving instance first. NativeInterop scope Borrow the owning device, queues, command list/buffer and native images. Define states/layouts on entry and exit, queue ownership and SDK completion. Restore heap/pipeline bindings after SDK evaluation. ShaderCapabilities Feature-selected shader variants for ray query and ray pipelines; explicit compiler and target versions. Compile probes must use the actual pinned Slang/DXC versions. ResourceRegistry Track native object metadata behind GPU allocations/texture handles, including usage, aliasing, views, owner queue and retire fence. Failure handling Unsupported feature diagnostics, device loss, SDK startup failure and fallback reconstruction must produce a usable error or supported rendering mode. Maintain these as a small, tested fork or upstreamable extension rather than scattering native calls throughout the renderer. records.text: ve SDK use must share the actual graphics device and resource ownership; introducing an unrelated second device is not a transparent shortcut. NoGraphicsAPI is the Vulkan device/resource/submission foundation of the current renderer. Basix adds native Vulkan adapters for acceleration structures, ray-query shader pipelines and optional Streamline interoperation. The current PT and guide path is a mixed implementation; no percentage of engine work or claim that every GPU allocation/dispatch passes through NoGraphicsAPI is supported. Responsibility Current owner / implementation Device and submission ownership NoGraphicsAPI creates the Vulkan device, command pools and timeline semaphores; Basix owns the session/lifetime policy and uses its submission/completion API. General shader data and textures NoGraphicsAPI heaps, textures and texture/sampler descriptor heaps hold the pointer-root data and native image resources used by the adapters. BLAS / TLAS / build scratch Basix native Vulkan acceleration-structure adapter creates these objects and native buffers/memory, including vkAllocateMemory. These allocations are not all NoGraphicsAPI heap allocations. PT and guide compute pipelines Basix NativePipeline creates Vulkan pipeline/layout/AS descriptor bindings, records vkCmdBindPipeline/vkCmdBindDescriptorSets and actual vkCmdDispatch on the borrowed native command buffer. NoGraphicsAPI owns that command buffer’s pool/submission lifetime. Upload, readback and fallback compute NoGraphicsAPI compute/resource operations are used for these stages; this does not make the separate native RT/guide dispatch its compute-pipeline API. Optional DLSS Original Basix adapters expose the same device/native Vulkan image and command metadata to Streamline. NVIDIA supplies the separately licensed SDK implementation/runtime. Rendering algorithms and checks Original Basix materials, PT sampling, world metadata, authored orientation, error policies, guide math and independent acceptance tools. NoGraphicsAPI supplies backend primitives rather than these algorithms. Implementation audit: owner, native buffers and NativePipeline · guide dispatch and renderer/SDK conversion . This describes the current Vulkan path; future backend refactoring remains a separate decision.

records.text: PETAFAB: what the public evidence supports Aaltonen’s technology page explicitly links PETAFAB to a custom NoGraphicsAPI engine, distance-field ray tracing, mesh shaders and Clayfield-derived matter/fluid simulation. It describes fully destructible SDF environments and large bot crowds. The author reports native 4K/240 FPS on RTX 4080 and other device figures; those results lack a reproduced test protocol here and are not comparable to a general triangle-based path tracer. Steam lists November 6, 2026, so the game is still upcoming at this research date. S05 · S06 Transferable lessons · analytical Choose the world representation around gameplay. An SDF world can make boolean destruction and ray marching natural, while mesh shaders serve other geometry workloads. A specialized representation and bounded art direction can outperform a general renderer without implying equal coverage of every material and scene type. For Basix, retain triangle geometry as the general asset path. Prototype SDF volumes only if destruction is a game requirement. A hybrid could render static/animated meshes conventionally and intersect destructible SDF chunks through procedural RT primitives, with explicit bounds and conservative distance steps. This is a proposed experiment, not a disclosed PETAFAB implementation. Unanswered implementation questions The examined public pages do not establish its hardware RT acceleration strategy, full light-transport estimator, denoiser, DLSS integration, source-code license, SDF resolution/streaming or worst-case destruction cost. Do not infer those from “ray tracing” or from footage. SDF ray marching and DXR triangle traversal are different mechanisms; neither phrase proves full Monte Carlo path tracing.

records.text: Proposed engine and frame architecture Assets → deterministic cooker → meshes / textures / materials / scene cells GPU scene + residency → visibility / G-buffer + BLAS / TLAS Hybrid: stochastic DI + diffuse GI / reflections PT: shared BSDF + light sampling + multi-bounce transport Guides → fallback denoising or optional DLSS RR → post → UI → presentation Proposed data flow. Raster and ray paths share asset identity and material semantics; reconstruction owns its history. Modules: Platform (window/input/files), Core (jobs/allocators/diagnostics), Assets (import/cook/cache), World (entities/transforms/animation/streaming), Render (GPU scene/materials/frame graph), GPU (NoGraphicsAPI plus extensions), Integrations (optional SDK adapters), and Tools (inspector/capture/profiling). Keep gameplay and physics outside rendering dependencies. Choose audio, physics and asset libraries only after separate license and integration checks. Frame ownership and scheduling Freeze a render snapshot of scene transforms and material/light tables. Upload changes into fence-protected ranges. Schedule animation/deformation, BLAS updates and TLAS construction before rays consume them. Cull visibility with GPU work, render stable primary-surface guides, then run the selected lighting integrator. Supply the reconstruction path with an explicit camera/history epoch. Retire descriptors, memory and acceleration structures after their last consumer completes. A render graph should declare reads/writes and external SDK boundaries even if the low-level API exposes global barriers. The graph can enforce ordering, transient resource reuse and memory peaks. Cross-queue overlap is a measured optimization: simultaneous AS construction, streaming and lighting may contend for bandwidth rather than shorten the frame. D3D12 decision A native D3D12 backend is strategically useful for PIX, DXR and Linear Algebra experiments, but it is a second implementation project. SM6.6 descriptor indexing provides bindless resources, not arbitrary shader pointer traversal. Use a logical GpuRef abstraction: Vulkan may encode a device pointer; D3D12 can encode a buffer/arena index plus byte offset behind typed access helpers. Shared structures must not silently reinterpret one encoding as the other. S16 Build a compile-and-dispatch ABI spike before promising one source path across DXIL/SPIR-V/Metal. Backend-specific access helpers may be necessary. If D3D12 must ship first, accept this abstraction work immediately

records.text: RT and PT quality: establish correctness first RTXPT’s main sample uses unified path tracing; its separate IntroSample demonstrates incremental hybrid rendering. It is useful as a reference for architecture, guides and validation, but its known issues distinguish D3D12 from Vulkan and include vendor-specific failures. Its framework and SDK dependency tree should not be copied wholesale into an MIT engine. S18 · S29 Proposed common foundation Implement one BSDF library for raster evaluation, direct-light sampling and ray hits. Begin with diffuse and GGX reflection, metallic/roughness textures, emissive surfaces, normal maps and double-sided rules. Use consistent units and exposure. Add a basic progressive reference integrator with next-event estimation, multiple importance sampling and Russian roulette; retain an accumulation mode without temporal reuse, neural reconstruction or radiance caches. Validate energy conservation, PDF normalization, sampling versus evaluation, and furnace behavior. Test transmission, volumes and hair later with their own reference scenes. Use scale-aware ray origin offsets, robust intersection handling and ray-cone or differential-based texture LOD. Primary visibility must agree with the RT scene on alpha testing, LOD, deformation and material identity. Geometry is a separate budget Static BLAS can be built once and compacted; deforming meshes require update or rebuild policies chosen by quality and traversal cost. Refit is not always faster overall. Track scratch peaks, TLAS instance counts, animation cost and allocation churn. Simplified RT proxies can make shadows/reflections diverge from raster detail. Visualize that divergence directly and budget higher RT detail for hero objects and mirrors. S10 Realtime evolution · proposal Establish a low-sample PT baseline, then add temporal denoising and optional RR. Introduce reservoir sampling, caches and SER one at a time against reference captures. Any radiance cache needs invalidation for moving geometry and lighting. Prefer predictable quality degradation and a hybrid fallback over assuming full PT will meet every device’s frame budget.

records.title: Summary and lessons learned
records.page: Basix Engine · Rendering research Two numerical evaluation paths Ray-spawn coordinate and uncertainty pipeline Two geometry paths and an independent boundary oracle Shared geometry with per-instance identity and orientation Arithmetic and hardware-policy evidence stay separate Same-device renderer inputs and optional SDK output flow
records.text: Summary and lessons learned What mattered: the API abstraction and the renderer are different projects. NoGraphicsAPI provides a compact model; Basix now proves one Vulkan hardware-ray-query seam while SDK texture interoperability remains open. PETAFAB supports the value of specialization; it does not establish general-purpose triangle PT performance. UE’s many-light quality also depends on scene representation and reconstruction. Practical consequence: test RT → native resource tagging → reconstruction before building an editor or virtualized geometry system. Share material/scene semantics between hybrid and PT paths. Treat geometry residency, sample selection and temporal quality as independent budgets. License consequence: the requested MIT core is practical, but the requested NVIDIA stack cannot all become MIT. Preserve a functional default without proprietary SDKs and publish the exact dependency/license manifest for each optional distribution. Limits: local correctness experiments are narrow; no cross-vendor benchmarks or shipping legal review were performed. DXR2/UE6 dates and preview APIs may change.
